_comment: #796: single source of truth for this repo's branch-protection settings.
CI runs on every PR and push to main/develop, but until #796 nothing
ENFORCED it: `develop` (the default branch, where all work lands) had no
protection object at all, and `main` had one with no required_status_checks
key — so a red CI run blocked nothing anywhere. This file plus
scripts/apply-branch-protection.sh turns that advisory signal into a gate,
and keeps the applied settings reviewable in git instead of living only in
the repo's web UI where drift is invisible.
`required_contexts` MUST match the `name:` of every job in
.github/workflows/ci.yml exactly. A required context that names a job that
no longer exists is never reported, so it stays forever-pending and blocks
EVERY pull request. tests/branch_protection.rs asserts the two lists are
equal so a job rename fails the test suite instead of wedging the queue.
Apply with:  scripts/apply-branch-protection.sh
Audit with:  scripts/apply-branch-protection.sh --check
Release branch. Only ever receives the develop -> main release PR, so
`strict` (branch must be up to date with base before merging) costs
nothing and guarantees the release commit was tested as it will land.
Default branch, receiving many concurrent agent branches. `strict` is
deliberately false: with strict on, every branch would need a rebase
and a full re-run each time another one landed, serialising the merge
queue for no real safety gain.
enforce_admins:false is #796's recommended option (c), pending the repo
owner's sign-off: the gate binds the PR merge button and any non-admin
push, while the owner keeps a deliberate escape hatch — a direct push
using CLAUDE.md's 'Path A' merge-locally-and-push path.
